the expression of the Star NAT is stimulated by cAMP and that the Star NAT downregulates the expression of the sense Star transcripts.
Star NAT expression is regulated by gonadotropins and that antisense RNA regulates steroid biosynthesis.

In summary, our research is concerned with
understanding the regulation of steroidogenic genes, particularly the Star gene, and its role in steroidogenesis.
the identification of new NATs and the elucidation of their role in the regulation of gene expression in steroidogenic cells.
the regulation of the steroidogenic acute regulatory (StAR) protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
antisense transcription of StAR may be a mechanism to control the levels of StA protein and the production of steroids.
the Star NAT is a novel and unique regulator of steroidogenesis that is expressed in a tissue-specific manner and is regulated by cAMP.
the antisense RNA to StAR (STAR NAT) regulates StAR expression and function by a yet unknown mechanism.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Star NAT is a hormone-regulated transcript that is complementary to Star and that may be involved in the regulation and/or stability of Star mRNA.
the expression of Star NAT in MA-10 mouse tumor Leydig cells is regulated by cAMP and it has an inhibitory effect on the expression and function of StAR.
the antisense transcript is a negative regulator of the sense transcript, which is consistent with the fact that the Star NAT contains a polyadenylation signal in the antisense direction.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the antisense Star NAT transcript is a novel regulator of Star expression and steroidogenesis in MA-10 mouse tumor Leydig cells.
antisense transcription is a new mechanism involved in the post-transcriptional regulation of StAR expression.
the Star NAT may have a negative effect on the expression and activity of StAR protein.
